title: Division 855 — capital gains and foreign residents
summary: Foreign residents disregard capital gains and losses unless the CGT asset is taxable Australian property (TAP) — direct or indirect interests in Australian real property, or assets used through an Australian permanent establishment. The TAP classification (s 855-15 table) is the boundary: real property (855-20), indirect interests (855-25 with the non-portfolio and principal asset tests), PE assets (855-35 reduction), options/rights, and fixed-trust interests (855-40). Subdiv 855-B handles becoming an Australian resident: market value cost base reset (855-45, subject to TAP and pre-1985 exceptions), trust becoming resident (855-50) and CFCs (855-55 via ITAA 1936 ss 411-414). Subsection coverage: operative 855-10(1)-(2), 855-15, 855-20, 855-25(1)-(2), 855-30, 855-32, 855-35(1)-(3), 855-40(1)-(3), 855-45(1)-(3), 855-50(1)-(2), 855-55(1)-(4) mapped to nodes; 855-5 (objects), 855-16 (definition), 855-1 (guide) contextual.

nodes.label: A foreign resident (or trustee of a foreign trust for CGT purposes) is a party to a CGT event
nodes.body: Division 855 lets foreign residents disregard capital gains and losses unless the underlying CGT asset is taxable Australian property (TAP) — a direct or indirect interest in Australian real property, or an asset used in a business carried on through an Australian permanent establishment. Special rules apply to individuals who were Australian residents (Subdiv 104-I) and to fixed trust interests.

nodes.label: Is the CGT asset taxable Australian property (TAP)?
nodes.body: TAP has 5 categories (s 855-15 table): (1) taxable Australian real property (s 855-20); (2) an indirect Australian real property interest (s 855-25) not covered by item 5; (3) a CGT asset used at any time in carrying on a business through an Australian permanent establishment (see s 855-16 for the PE article meaning); (4) an option or right to acquire an asset covered by items 1-3; (5) an interest held by a foreign resident in an entity that is an indirect Australian real property interest that is not an asset covered by item 2 because of the section 855-25(2) exception.

nodes.label: Gain or loss is disregarded (s 855-10)
nodes.body: If the CGT asset is not TAP, the capital gain or loss from the CGT event is disregarded — the foreign resident has no Australian CGT exposure on that asset. This is the core Div 855 relief.

nodes.label: Is the asset taxable Australian real property (real property in Australia, or mining/quarrying/prospecting rights)?
nodes.body: Taxable Australian real property is real property situated in Australia (including a lease of land) or a mining, quarrying or prospecting right (to the extent not real property) where the minerals, petroleum or quarry materials are in Australia (s 855-20).

nodes.label: Is the asset an indirect Australian real property interest (membership interests in an entity)?
nodes.body: A membership interest is an indirect Australian real property interest if it passes both the non-portfolio interest test (s 960-195: 10%+ of the entity's membership interests) and the principal asset test (s 855-30: the market value of the entity's taxable Australian real property exceeds the market value of all its other assets) — ss 855-25(1)(a)-(b). The 12-month lookback applies (interest must pass the tests now, or throughout a 12-month period ending within the last 24 months).

nodes.label: Did you use the asset at any time in carrying on a business through an Australian permanent establishment?
nodes.body: An asset used at any time in carrying on a business through an Australian PE is TAP (s 855-15 item 3), using the DTA permanent establishment article meaning (s 855-16). Note s 855-35 reduces the gain/loss proportionally if the asset was only used for the PE business for part of the ownership period.

nodes.label: Gain is assessable / loss can be claimed — normal CGT rules apply
nodes.body: TAP assets of foreign residents remain in the Australian CGT net. The gain is included in assessable income (Div 102) and the loss is available under the normal rules. For indirect interests, the entity-level asset test catches interests in entities whose value is principally derived from Australian real property.

nodes.label: Is the asset your main residence (which would otherwise be exempt under Div 118-B)?
nodes.body: A foreign resident's main residence is generally not exempt under Div 118-B (the main residence exemption is limited for foreign residents — see s 118-110(4)-(5) and transitional rules). Special choice rules in s 855-35 area and the s 118-110 modifications apply. This is the interaction node: even TAP status does not revive the main residence exemption for most foreign residents.

nodes.label: Are you a foreign resident beneficiary of a fixed trust with an interest in a CGT asset that is not TAP?
nodes.body: s 855-40 provides comparable treatment for indirect ownership through a fixed trust: a gain in respect of your interest in a fixed trust is disregarded if the asset would not have been TAP had you held it directly (subject to conditions in ss 855-40(2)-(3)).

nodes.label: You become an Australian resident (Subdiv 855-B)
nodes.body: When an individual or company becomes an Australian resident, CGT assets owned just before that time get a market value cost base reset (s 855-45), subject to exceptions. This is a separate trigger from the Subdiv 855-A foreign-resident disposal rules.

statute.title: Individual or company becomes an Australian resident

rulings.title: 855-45(3) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997

nodes.label: Is the asset taxable Australian property, or was it acquired before 20 September 1985?
nodes.body: The cost base reset in s 855-45 does not apply to assets that are already TAP (they keep their existing cost base) or pre-CGT assets acquired before 20 September 1985. The reset applies to all other CGT assets owned just before becoming an Australian resident.

rulings.title: 855-45(3) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997

nodes.label: Reset the first element of cost base / reduced cost base to market value at the residence change time
nodes.body: On becoming an Australian resident, the first element of the cost base and reduced cost base of each qualifying CGT asset becomes its market value at that time (s 855-45(2)). Note the effect is subject to s 768-950 (temporary residents) and does not apply to CFCs — s 855-55 applies instead, modifying the treatment via ITAA 1936 ss 411-414.

nodes.label: Is the entity a trust that becomes a resident trust, or a CFC that becomes an Australian resident?
nodes.body: s 855-50 deals with trusts that become resident trusts (market value reset of trustee assets, mirroring s 855-45). s 855-55 deals with CFCs that become Australian residents — s 855-45 does NOT apply; instead the ITAA 1936 ss 411-414 modifications apply to the CFC's assets.
